Name: Allosaurus
Description: A huge, swift hunter, the allosaurus measures 30 feet in length and weighs 10,000 pounds.

Name: Ankylosaurus

Name: Antelope
Description: A typical antelope stands a bit less than 3 feet at the shoulder, measures 4 feet in length, and weighs 60 pounds.

Name: Archelon
Description: An ancient relative of the smaller leatherback sea turtle, the archelon can grow up to 13 feet long and 16 feet from flipper to flipper.

Name: Arsinoitherium

Name: Badger

Name: Baluchitherium

Name: Basilosaurus

Name: Bat

Name: Bison (common)

Name: Boar (common)

Name: Brachiosaurus

Name: Camel

Name: Canary

Name: Cat (common)

Name: Cat (hunting)

Name: Cat (Osirian wise-eye)

Name: Cattle

Name: Centipede (house)

Name: Cheetah

Name: Chicken

Name: Compsognathus

Name: Constrictor snake
Description: Be they jungle-dwelling pythons or swamp-dwelling boas like the anaconda, constrictor snakes are among the most deadly predatory animals of the tropical wilds.

Name: Crab

Name: Crimson whale
Description: While many cetaceans are docile, the crimson whale is an aggressive hunter that evolved to quickly kill even the largest and most powerful of prey.

Name: Crocodile
Description: This reptile lunges out of the placid water with shocking speed. Its jaw gapes open in a roar, its powerful tail lashing behind.

Name: Deinonychus
Description: As swift and agile as it is deadly, the deinonychus is a pack hunter, running with several of its kind to take down prey and rip it apart with their gutting talons.

Name: Dimetrodon
Description: A dimetrodon is a quadrupedal reptile similar in shape to a crocodile, but with a blunter snout filled with jagged, sharp teeth.

Name: Dire ape
Description: Known to many scholars as the gigantopithecus, the dire ape is a much more dangerous and bestial creature than the relatively peaceful gorilla.

Name: Dire badger
